description.fun: Despite the name, Sandshrew is more armadillo or pangolin than shrew: it curls into a tight ball to survive falls and attacks, and spends most of its time in deep burrows. Its dry hide soaks up water efficiently, which suits desert life, but if it gets too wet its skin goes wrinkly and it has to dry off near a volcano or with a sand bath.
description.guide: A small Ground Pokémon resembling a pangolin or armadillo, with a tough, dry hide and sharp claws for digging. It lives in deep burrows in deserts and caves and curls into a ball to protect itself. Its Alolan form is an Ice and Steel type covered in a shell of ice and steel.
description.tagline: A desert pangolin that rolls into a ball when trouble comes

description.fun: Volcanic activity drove Alola's Sandshrew up into the snowy mountains, where they grew a hard shell of ice and steel. It can't curl into a ball any more, and at festivals Alolans hold contests to see who can slide one farthest across the ice.

Sandslash's quills and claws break off easily but grow back fast, and it sheds them regularly; the broken pieces have even been carved into plows for farm fields. It's a good climber, ambushing foes from the trees and slashing down Berries for the Sandshrew waiting below. When danger comes, it curls into a spiky ball and rolls.
description.guide: The evolution of Sandshrew, a pangolin-like Ground Pokémon with a back covered in sharp quills and long claws for slashing and digging. It curls into a ball to roll or protect itself and is a skilled tree climber. Its Alolan form is an Ice and Steel type with icy quills.
description.tagline: A spiky pangolin that drops Berries, and ambushes, from the trees

description.fun: Its steel quills are coated in ice and stand tall like icicles, and its long, hooked claws work like ice axes. Faster than any other Pokémon in the snowy mountains, it draws climbers hoping to see its spikes sparkle at dawn.
